title: Commissioning Compass: original assessment
description: Assess commissioning across eight aspects with 79 questions and 89 factors. Record scores, evidence, actions, and reviews.
introduction: The system assessment is structured around the eight aspects of commissioning. Use each as a lens, compare what different people can see, and move from assessment to action.

source.title: Scoring sheet for your Commissioning Compass: system assessment for change
source.note: The original assessment is transcribed from the unfilled 24 March 2026 scoring-sheet master: eight aspect descriptors, 79 assessment questions, 89 constraints and enablers, initial and revised aspect scores, and initial and final question scores /100. The source score bands and wording are preserved; layout whitespace is normalised. The online edition adds perspective comparison, saving, decisions, and reviews. The Teachable course has further teaching, approaches, cases, and resources beyond the scoring sheet.

scoreBands: 50 – 74 Good (opportunities identified/issues need to be addressed)
instructions: Scoring sheet for your Commissioning Compass: system assessment for change
System Assessment using the Eight aspects of commissioning

For your system assessment, you need to score your system on how it is performing on each of the eight aspects of commissioning. First, we will carry out an initial overall score, and then we will do an in depth assessment on each of the eight aspects of commissioning.
Give your system an initial score
Give your place an instinctive score on how you are doing in terms of each of the 'eight aspects'. Do this quickly. It is just your first pass, your gut reaction.
We will encourage you to revisit this after working through the questions for the aspects.
Scores are categorised as below. Note that scores of 70 and above have been rare in system-assessments so far.
0 – 24 Poor (significant risk)
25 – 49 Fair (lesser/lower risk, improvement required)
50 – 74 Good (opportunities identified/issues need to be addressed)
75 – 100 Excellent (no action required)
Now carry out your full system assessment
Next, work through the full system assessment. For each of the eight aspects, you have two scoring sheets below.
System Assessment questions
Factors that constrain and enable
The system assessment questions: These encourage you to take a deeper look at your system and develop more curiosity. Score your 'system' on each question using the scoring system:
0 – 24 Poor (significant risk)
25 – 49 Fair (lesser/lower risk, improvement required)
50 – 74 Good (opportunities identified/issues need to be addressed)
75 – 100 Excellent (no action required)

If you are doing this as a team and each person scored individually, do not simply average your results – look at the overall pattern of highs and lows, open up the conversation about what people are seeing in the system to give that score.

In a workshop, this can be a great way to use appreciative or action enquiry. It will help you to be curious about how stakeholders experience each aspect and what the knock-on impact of that is. This will help too with the next step.
At the end, we’ll compare your initial gut reactions to your actual score. Again, we ask you to be curious about where there are differences or alignment. What is that telling you?

Factors that constrain and enable: For each aspect, you are provided with a list of 'factors in place that constrain and enable'. These are important influences on your commissioning, some of which may be blockers (constraints) and others of which may provide opportunities or advantages (enablers). Which hold you/ the system back? Which supports you most to achieve change and outcomes?
Your key question is: Select the three greatest enablers and the three greatest constraints.

Be curious about the depth of your awareness or understanding of each of the factors. You may wish to explore the factors further before you score them, but this is not essential at this stage. You can pick that up in your action plan later.
Once you have discussed each of the factors that constrain and enable, select the three most important enablers and the three most important constraints for each of the eight aspects.

If undertaking this assessment with stakeholders, it is likely that there will be very different perspectives in the system. In your workshops, think about how you can explore these perspectives to give you a deeper understanding of your system relationships. There are not right and wrong answers here. This is to provide you with insight and intelligence to identify where to intervene for the most effective change.

sections.title: Citizen, place, and outcome centred
sections.description: Citizens in charge of their own outcomes, with success measured by people’s views on whether and to what extent they can live their lives well

questions.label: Initial aspect score
questions.prompt: Citizens in charge of their own outcomes, with success measured by people’s views on whether and to what extent they can live their lives well

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt: Is the work led by the people or place who need it, and measured according to the outcomes they get?

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt: Are we commissioning and working together in a way that drives real change on the ground, as measured by real impact and reported by citizens and communities?

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt: Are we taking outcomes-led approaches, learning from real change on the ground, tracking and learning from impact, and reports from citizens and communities?

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt: Do we have real engagement with and understanding of actual needs, demand as different from need, including active identification of unmet needs or unmet demand? For economy, infrastructure, citizens and community, seeking to identify real needs rather than our belief about what is needed?

questions.label: Question 5
questions.prompt: Are equity and sustainability at the heart of our commissioning approach?

questions.label: Question 6
questions.prompt: Do we have co-production, co-design, or engagement at all stages of the commissioning cycle? Do we know when to use each type?

questions.label: Question 7
questions.prompt: Do we have a commitment to co-producing analysis, design, decision-making, delivery, and governance with all citizens, stakeholders, promoting inclusion and equality, especially from underrepresented groups?

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt: Do we look at the whole experience of from the citizen community side, as opposed to a narrow organisational, structural, service, or process silo?

questions.label: Question 9
questions.prompt: Are we making access to interventions, support and infrastructure clear and accessible to all? Including those who wish to pay?

questions.label: Question 10
questions.prompt: Are we influencing the approach of the whole organisation and partners in a way consistent with citizen, community, and outcome-centred working?

sections.title: Information, insight, and innovation
sections.description: Commissioning that focuses on innovation and creativity and based on robust information / insight

questions.label: Initial aspect score
questions.prompt: Commissioning that focuses on innovation and creativity and based on robust information / insight

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt: Do we really understand all the needs in our place, including the unmet need?

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt: Do we have an ambitious and clear adaptive route map for change?

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt: Do we practice active learning and insight development?

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt: Do we have a culture of innovation, experiment, and learning from failure (and success)?

questions.label: Question 5
questions.prompt: Do we commission from a values-driven position, taking responsibility for outcomes while avoiding the ‘heroic’ mode of ‘fixing everything’ in favour of an enabling approach where people feel involved and part of designing and implementing things that matter to them? And we involve the workforce in design.

questions.label: Question 6
questions.prompt: Are we using approaches that harness complexity and an appreciation of whole systems?

questions.label: Question 7
questions.prompt: Do we work across different paradigms as appropriate, based on multiple perspectives?

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt: Do we have an understanding of great leadership of transformational change?

questions.label: Question 9

questions.label: Question 10
questions.prompt: Are quality, social value, and value for money evaluated proportionately and based on evidence?

questions.label: Question 11
questions.prompt: Do we have and share data from across the whole system, including identifying gaps and unmet needs that will result in demand?

questions.label: Question 12
questions.prompt: Do we seek external challenge, peer review, coaching, development, and reflective practice?

questions.label: Question 13
questions.prompt: Are we powerfully advocating for commissioning and leading by example?

sections.description: Technically excellent, clear, and robust arrangements

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt: Do we have a strong, effective process?

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt: Are you balancing meeting urgent financial and other priority requirements with thinking about long-term impacts?

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt: Does your commissioning process support good collaboration, market development and co-operation, competition for improvement, value for money and commercials, and clarity of types of contracting improvement?

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt: How do you relate your timeliness of engagement in your strategic commissioning process? Do you balance time on co-production, design, market/ provider co-design, specification development, contract management, learning, etc?

questions.prompt: Do you have a positive approach to types and design of procurement and commissioning that focuses on proportionality and matches design and the outcomes sought?

questions.label: Question 7

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt: Are you able to maintain a strong commissioning process even in joint and share commissioning and shared arrangements?

reviewQuestions: What changed in people’s lived experience?
What did we learn about how the system behaves?
What did we learn about our arrangements, rules, measures, relationships and forms of help?
What did this reveal about who we think we are, what we think we are here for, and whose purposes count?
